models.title: Single-product break-even quantity with positive contribution margin
models.summary: Continuous sales volume at which revenue covers fixed and proportional variable expenses in the specified interval. A conditional cost-accounting calculation; it neither predicts sales nor establishes feasible capacity.

relationship.original_equation: Break-even units = total fixed costs / contribution margin per unit; unit contribution margin = unit selling price - variable cost per unit.
relationship.locator: Section 3.2 opening assumptions, Figure 3.4 and Hicks contribution-margin statement
relationship.translation_notes: Introduced F,p,v,Q_be map the source prose quantities. Substitution of the source-defined per-unit margin into its break-even formula yields one atomic relation. Dimensions currency/(currency/U)=U. No rounding/ceiling operator: output is the exact continuous threshold. For indivisible units a distinct ceiling rule is needed to find the first integer reaching nonnegative income, and an exact zero-income integer may not exist. F=0 is admitted as the algebraic no-fixed-expense boundary. Price must exceed variable cost; equality or a loss per unit does not define this finite positive-margin threshold.

variables.definition: Total fixed expenses assigned to this product/service and accounting interval within the relevant range.
variables.context: Same single homogeneous product/service, enterprise and accounting interval; current USD basis and same expense scope, with constant unit selling price and variable unit cost across the stated relevant volume range; no inventory change for manufactured units. Parameters must be measured for this regime.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative; zero explicitly admits no fixed expense; not a fixed cost per unit.

variables.source_symbol: Introduced p = Sales Price per Unit
variables.definition: Constant sales revenue earned per homogeneous unit sold on the specified monetary basis.
variables.context: Same single homogeneous product/service, enterprise and accounting interval; current USD basis and same expense scope, with constant unit selling price and variable unit cost across the stated relevant volume range; no inventory change for manufactured units. Parameters must be measured for this regime.
variables.domain: Finite; p>v>=0, so p is positive. No discounts or changing price over volume.

variables.source_symbol: Introduced v = Variable Cost per Unit
variables.definition: All variable expenses per unit sold, including variable selling expenses when included in operating-income boundary.
variables.context: Same single homogeneous product/service, enterprise and accounting interval; current USD basis and same expense scope, with constant unit selling price and variable unit cost across the stated relevant volume range; no inventory change for manufactured units. Parameters must be measured for this regime.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative, constant within declared range; independently supplied, never a reusable material default.

variables.source_symbol: Introduced Q_be = Break-Even Point in Units
variables.definition: Continuous units sold during the accounting interval at zero operating income under the source cost profile.
variables.context: Same single homogeneous product/service, enterprise and accounting interval; current USD basis and same expense scope, with constant unit selling price and variable unit cost across the stated relevant volume range; no inventory change for manufactured units. Parameters must be measured for this regime.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative; valid as feasible operating volume only if within relevant range/capacity.

assumptions: Source assumptions: costs can be separated into fixed and proportional variable components; per-unit price and variable cost are constant in the relevant range.
Source assumption: for manufacturing, units produced are sold and inventory does not change. Application profile: a single product/service; no varying sales mix.
Application boundary: operating-income break-even using the stated expense classifications, not financing cash flow or after-tax profit.
limitations: A volume outside relevant capacity/range is not a defensible operating result; scalar guards cannot check metadata about that range.
No inference about demand, sales realizability, profit maximization, future profitability or investment desirability.
Indivisible-unit rounding and exact multi-product mix calculations are outside this scalar relation.

models.inverse_notes: Given Q_be,p,v, F=Q_be*(p-v), with Q_be>=0 and p>v>=0; no denominator. Given positive Q_be,F and v, p=v+F/Q_be; requires F>0 to satisfy original p>v. Similarly v=p-F/Q_be, require Q_be>0,F>0,0<=v<p. Substitution: Q_be=225,p=100,v=20 gives F=18000 and forward 225. At F=Q_be=0, any p>v>=0 is compatible, so prices/costs are not identified. With F=0 and Q_be>0 no solution under p>v. p=v,F=0 would yield zero income at every volume, but is excluded from this unique-threshold profile. Target-profit and general operating-income inversions are not returned as new clones.

gaps: New fixed_cost, unit_variable_cost and break_even_quantity meanings; unit_price reuses b01 definition with matching sale-price scope. Homogeneous-unit arithmetic and relevant-range metadata required; USD alone does not make runtime-ready.

models.title: Linear mixed cost within a relevant activity range
models.summary: Total of one defined cost pool with fixed and proportional activity components. The pool may be a component such as an occupancy tax or an entire explicitly covered expense set; no automatic equivalence to total enterprise production cost.

relationship.original_equation: Y = a + b*x, where Y is total mixed cost, a fixed cost, b variable cost per unit and x activity level.
relationship.locator: Section 2.2, Mixed Costs and Stepped Costs, Ocean Breeze and equation following Figure 2.19
relationship.translation_notes: Introduced C_pool=source Y, F=a, v=b; x unchanged. Activity unit A is the declared driver (e.g. occupied room-night), not necessarily product count or elapsed time. Dimensions currency + (currency/A)*A = currency. Source reference is a monthly flow of tax costs: x accumulates occupied room-nights, not rooms available or capital stock. Nonnegative-cost profile admits zero fixed/variable amounts. A generic linear model is conditional; it does not estimate a or b or license extrapolation beyond relevant range.

Application profile: nonnegative expense pool on a consistent accounting basis; no rebates or signed credits treated as expenses.

models.inverse_notes: Solve F=C_pool-v*x, requiring recovered F>=0; solve v=(C_pool-F)/x only for x>0 and v>=0; solve x=(C_pool-F)/v only for v>0 and x>=0, within relevant range. Published substitution C_pool=2300,F=2000,x=60 gives v=5 and forward 2300. At x=0,C_pool=F, v is unrestricted nonnegative; unequal C_pool,F gives no solution. At v=0,C_pool=F every admissible x fits; otherwise no solution. Inverses infer arithmetic consistency, not a cost-driver causal mechanism or estimated parameters.

gaps: New cost-pool, driver and per-driver meanings/units required; pool scope must not be coerced into total_production_cost or a product unit. Definition distinct from electricity-cost because generic mixed cost includes fixed portion and a declared activity driver.

models.title: Average total production cost
models.summary: Total production cost allocated per homogeneous unit produced. Applies to nonlinear as well as linear costs and is distinct from the cost of an additional unit.

relationship.locator: Section 7.3, Average and Marginal Costs, equation AC=TC/Q and Table 7.8
relationship.translation_notes: Symbols retained. Dimensions currency/U. No assumption of linear total cost, no averaging over calendar periods, and no use of a price or marginal-cost input. The cost boundary must distinguish accounting outlays from economic opportunity costs; this record does not silently choose between them or relabel one as the other. Zero total cost is an admitted mathematical boundary of the nonnegative-cost profile for positive output; zero output has no defined per-unit average.

variables.definition: All production costs assigned to the same output and interval under the declared cost convention.

variables.context: Same enterprise, homogeneous output, production interval and cost boundary; TC covers all costs of that production under a declared accounting or economic cost convention, consistently used throughout. Q is units produced, not units sold unless independently matched.

models.title: Unit contribution margin
models.summary: Per-unit sales revenue remaining after all matching variable costs, available toward fixed expenses and then operating income. Negative values retain a per-unit shortfall rather than being silently clipped.

relationship.original_equation: Unit contribution margin = per-unit sales price - variable cost per unit.
relationship.locator: Section 3.1, Unit Contribution Margin; Hicks examples; Margin at the Kiosk
relationship.translation_notes: Introduced p,v,cm map source prose labels. Dimensions currency/U - currency/U = currency/U. This independently named accounting quantity is a definition, not a separate multiplication stage or a synonym for profit: fixed costs remain unpaid. Nonnegative price/cost profile permits p<v and signed cm; source calls it a difference, while positive examples do not justify silently restricting margin to positive. No assertion of volume invariance outside a declared constant-price/cost regime.

variables.source_symbol: Introduced p = Per Unit Sales Price
variables.definition: Sales revenue per homogeneous unit sold.
variables.context: Same sold product/service unit, transaction/interval, price quality/currency basis and complete variable-expense scope. Unit variable expense includes the costs triggered by that sale under the chosen contribution-income definition; fixed expenses are excluded.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative; free-sale boundary p=0 admitted for the accounting difference.

variables.source_symbol: Introduced v = Variable Cost per Unit
variables.definition: Complete variable expense per same unit sold.
variables.context: Same sold product/service unit, transaction/interval, price quality/currency basis and complete variable-expense scope. Unit variable expense includes the costs triggered by that sale under the chosen contribution-income definition; fixed expenses are excluded.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative; includes all applicable variable selling/production expenses.

variables.source_symbol: Introduced cm = Contribution Margin per Unit
variables.definition: Signed selling-price excess over all per-unit variable costs, before fixed expenses.
variables.context: Same sold product/service unit, transaction/interval, price quality/currency basis and complete variable-expense scope. Unit variable expense includes the costs triggered by that sale under the chosen contribution-income definition; fixed expenses are excluded.
variables.domain: Finite signed, including zero and per-unit shortfall when negative.

assumptions: Source definition: compare the revenue from one unit with its variable cost; fixed expenses are outside the unit contribution margin.
Application profile: monetary price and variable cost are nonnegative on one consistent sales/expense basis.
limitations: Not gross margin based on absorption cost, net profit or a cash-flow return.
Does not identify demand or whether changes in price leave volume or unit costs unchanged.
